english.title: Reinstate a building / work removed etc in compliance with enforcement notice - TPA 1990
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without planning permission issued under the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, carried out development on land, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LAND..), by way of reinstating or restoring

(A)_[a building, namely **(..SPECIFY THE BUILDING..),]_
(B)_[buildings, namely **(..SPECIFY THE BUILDINGS..),]_
(C)_[works, namely **(..SPECIFY THE WORKS..),]_

which had been removed or altered in compliance with an enforcement notice issued under section 172 of the Act by **(..SPECIFY THE LOCAL PLANNING AUTHORITY ..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 181 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

english.notes:
Section 181(5)(b) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 provides:-
"no person shall be liable under any of the provisions of section 179(1) to (5) for failure to take any steps required to be taken by an enforcement notice by way of demolition or alteration of what has been so reinstated or restored."

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
